title: Patents for Humanity Program Improvement Act
official_summary:
Patents for Humanity Program Improvement Act

This bill authorizes the holder of an acceleration certificate awarded under the Patents for Humanity program to transfer the certificate to another party.

(The Patents for Humanity program recognizes patent owners, applicants, and licensees that use their inventions to meet humanitarian challenges. The winners each receive a certificate that can be used to accelerate certain U.S. Patent and Trademark Office proceedings, such as a patent application.)

summary.headline: A new law lets winners of the Patents for Humanity award pass their acceleration certificate to another party.
summary.what_it_does: The Patents for Humanity program honors patent owners, applicants, and licensees who use their inventions to meet humanitarian needs. Winners receive a certificate that can speed up certain U.S. Patent and Trademark Office proceedings, such as a patent application. This law allows the holder of that certificate to transfer it to someone else.

who_it_affects.how: They can now transfer their acceleration certificate to another party instead of keeping it themselves.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations or individuals who might receive a transferred certificate
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to use a certificate that someone else earned to speed up certain Patent Office proceedings.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2021. The summary does not state a separate effective date.
